title: Export Large Objects from Postgres
description:
It is really easy to write large files to Postgres using the function `postgresImportLargeObject()` (thanks to #472).
However, when the file is larger (eg 1GB+) it is hard to export the file again as one would have to use a query (and afaik fields are limited to 1GB), in fact I'm still trying to figure out how to get the file back out...

It would be great to have a `postgresExportLargeObject` function or similar which can download the file again.

Eg a simple example code is this (assumes a valid `con`):

```R
file <- "mytestfile.bin"
# generate a file with 800MB filesize using bash
# system(sprintf("dd if=/dev/urandom of=%s bs=1M count=800", file))
prettyunits::pretty_bytes(file.size(file))
#> [1] "838.86 MB"

# 1. Create Table =====
DBI::dbExecute(
  con,
  "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lo_tester (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    lo_link OID
  )"
)
"lo_tester" %in% DBI::dbListTables(con)
#> [1] TRUE

# 2. Insert Large Object =====
t0 <- Sys.time()
DBI::dbWithTransaction(con, {
  oid <- RPostgres::postgresImportLargeObject(con, file)
  q <- sprintf(
    "INSERT INTO lo_tester (name, lo_link) VALUES ('%s', %d);",
    file,
    oid
  )
  DBI::dbExecute(con, q)
})
cat(sprintf("Inserting took %0.2fs\n", difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")))
#> Inserting took 144.86s

# inserted as oid
oid
#> [1] 557400

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM lo_tester;")
#>   id           name lo_link
#> 1  1 mytestfile.bin  557400


# 3. Fetch the data again ====
r <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT lo_get($1) as lo_data", params = list(oid))
#> Error: Failed to fetch row : ERROR:  invalid memory alloc request size 1677721603
```

Here postgresExportLargeObject could look like this `DBI::postgresExportLargeObject(con, oid, "mytestfile_out.bin")`.

Is this something that you would consider useful in the package?

title: "! Multiple queries must use the same column names." when issuing a query against a Postgres server running with the pg_duckdb extension
description:
Working with RPostgres against a postgres server with the pg_duckdb extension running in a container (image: pgduckdb/pgduckdb:17-v1.0.0), I can successfully make a connection and count the number of records in a parquet file:

```r
> library(RPostgres); library(DBI);
> con <- dbConnect(
    drv = RPostgres::Postgres(), 
    host = "<redacted>", 
    user = "<redacted>",
    password = "<redacted>", 
    dbname = "<redacted>"
  )
> "SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet('s3://us-prd-motherduck-open-datasets/netflix/netflix_daily_top_10.parquet')" |> 
+   dbGetQuery(conn = con)
  count
1  7100

```

When issuing another query to get the data in the file (this query works using pgsql) I get:

```r
> "SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://us-prd-motherduck-open-datasets/netflix/netflix_daily_top_10.parquet')" |> 
+   dbGetQuery(conn = con)
Error:
! Multiple queries must use the same column names.
Hide Traceback
     ▆
  1. ├─DBI::dbGetQuery(...)
  2. └─DBI::dbGetQuery(...)
  3.   └─DBI (local) .local(conn, statement, ...)
  4.     ├─DBI::dbSendQuery(conn, statement, ...)
  5.     └─RPostgres::dbSendQuery(conn, statement, ...)
  6.       └─RPostgres (local) .local(conn, statement, ...)
  7.         ├─methods::new(...)
  8.         │ ├─methods::initialize(value, ...)
  9.         │ └─methods::initialize(value, ...)
 10.         └─RPostgres:::result_create(conn@ptr, statement, immediate) 
```
I am not sure if this is an issue with the pg_duckdb extension for Postgres or whether I haven't understood how to use it properly, but since the same query works in pgsql CLI I was thinking maybe it could be related to RPostgres.

title: RPostgres uses libpq 13.20 which triggers errors connecting to Neondb
description:
I've been getting the same error as #476 when running `RPostgres::dbConnect()` on a Neondb that requires SSL connection. It seems that the precompiled Windows version of the package comes with `libpq` 13.20 which seems to be the culprit, unneccessarily requiring to provide an `sslrootcert` in the connection. Building from source seems to use the libpq version available from RTools according to #486 which for RTools 4.5 seems to be 13.20.

``` r
DBI::dbGetInfo(RPostgres::Postgres())
#> $driver.version
#> [1] '1.4.8'
#> 
#> $client.version
#> [1] '13.20'
```
I built the package by forcing to use the fallback version of libpq instead of RTools which installs libpq 15.12. Using this version I no longer have any issues.
``` r
DBI::dbGetInfo(RPostgres::Postgres())
#> $driver.version
#> [1] '1.4.7.9902'
#> 
#> $client.version
#> [1] '15.12'
```
Is there a workaround to use a newer version of libpq or to link it to an external version instead of the one included in RTools?

title: Expose SQLSTATE (and other diagnostic fields) on error conditions
description:
## Summary

When a query triggers a server-side error, RPostgres surfaces only the libpq
*message string* on the R condition. The SQLSTATE code and the other diagnostic
fields libpq exposes through `PQresultErrorField()` are discarded before the
error reaches R. As a result there is no reliable, locale-independent way to
classify an error programmatically.

It would be very useful if RPostgres carried at least the SQLSTATE onto the
condition.

## Why this matters

We define server-side validation in PL/pgSQL triggers and raise errors with
stable, explicit error codes:

```sql
RAISE EXCEPTION 'konto % ist nicht bebuchbar.', NEW.konto
  USING ERRCODE = 'FS002',
        HINT    = 'Setzen Sie bebuchbar = TRUE ...';
```

On the R side we want to branch on the *code* to drive the UI, precisely because
the message is user-facing, localized (German here), and may be reworded. The
code is the stable contract; the message is not.

Because only the message string reaches R, we are forced to recover the
classification by regex-matching the (German) message text:

```r
sqlstate <- if (grepl("ist nicht bebuchbar", msg, fixed = TRUE)) {
  "FS002"
} else if (grepl("nicht gültig", msg, fixed = TRUE)) {
  "FS001"
} else {
  NA_character_
}
```

This is brittle: it breaks if a message is reworded, it is locale-dependent, and
it cannot distinguish our raised codes from coincidentally similar text. The
`ERRCODE` we set on the server is the correct key to branch on — we just can't
read it back.

## Reproducible example

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())

err <- tryCatch(
  dbExecute(con, "DO $$ BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION 'boom' USING ERRCODE = 'FS002'; END $$;"),
  error = function(e) e
)

conditionMessage(err)
#> [1] "Failed to fetch row : ERROR:  boom\nCONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function inline_code_block line 1 at RAISE\n"

str(unclass(err))
#> List of 2
#>  $ message: chr "Failed to fetch row : ERROR:  boom\nCONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL ..."
#>  $ call   : NULL

class(err)
#> [1] "simpleError" "error"       "condition"
```

It is a plain `simpleError`: just `message` and `call`, no SQLSTATE field and no
SQLSTATE-derived class. The `'FS002'` code is gone. There is also no
`dbGetException()` fallback:

```r
existsMethod("dbGetException", "PqConnection")
#> [1] FALSE
```

## Where it's dropped

Every server-side error funnels through one helper, which keeps only
`PQerrorMessage()`:

```cpp
// src/DbConnection.cpp
void DbConnection::conn_stop(PGconn* conn, const char* msg) {
  cpp11::stop(std::string(msg) + " : " + PQerrorMessage(conn));
}
```

Result-level errors take the same path (`PqResultImpl::conn_stop` →
`DbConnection::conn_stop`), and `cpp11::stop()` raises a plain `simpleError` with
no extra fields. `PQresultErrorField` / `PG_DIAG_SQLSTATE` do not appear anywhere
in the source, so the SQLSTATE that libpq has on hand is never read.

## Desired behavior

Any of the following would solve it, in rough order of preference:

1. Attach the SQLSTATE as a field on a classed condition (e.g. `err$sqlstate`),
   and optionally give the condition an extra class such as
   `RPostgres_error_<sqlstate>` so handlers can dispatch directly:
   `tryCatch(..., RPostgres_error_FS002 = ...)`.
2. Additionally attach the other `PQresultErrorField()` diagnostics (detail,
   hint, column, constraint, table, schema, context) as fields, so callers don't
   have to parse them out of the message string.
3. At minimum, provide a `dbGetException()`-style accessor returning the SQLSTATE
   of the last error on the connection.

libpq already exposes everything needed via `PQresultErrorField(res, field)` —
`PG_DIAG_SQLSTATE`, `PG_DIAG_MESSAGE_DETAIL`, `PG_DIAG_MESSAGE_HINT`,
`PG_DIAG_COLUMN_NAME`, `PG_DIAG_TABLE_NAME`, `PG_DIAG_CONSTRAINT_NAME`, etc.
These would need to be read where the error result is turned into an R error,
and carried onto the condition rather than collapsed into a single string.

title: Error in dbConnect(): linux socket location moved
description:
I'm running Postgres 15 and the current CRAN RPostgres on debian 12. 
When I do:
```
> con <- dbConnect(Postgres())
```
I get the following:
```
Error: connection to server on socket "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432" failed: No such file or directory
        Is the server running locally and accepting connections on that socket?
```

I confirmed via psql that the database is running and accessible with current user.
Some poking around:
```$ netstat -nlp | grep 5432```
shows the socket at `/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432`

I was able to get a successful `dbConnect()` after doing:
```$ ln -s /var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432 /tmp```

``` r
q_list_types <- "

    t.typname AS type_name,
    CASE
        WHEN t.typtype = 'e' THEN 'ENUM'
        WHEN t.typtype = 'c' THEN 'COMPOSITE'
        WHEN t.typtype = 'd' THEN 'DOMAIN'
```

title: `dbAppendTable()` is incompatible with PostgreSQL row-level security enabled (COPY FROM not supported)
description:
Consider the following minimal reproducible example:

1. Create a table `public.test` with row-level security (RLS) enabled and a simple default-allow policy defined:
    
    ```sql
    CREATE TABLE public.test (
      "id"  integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
      title text
    );
    
    ALTER TABLE public.test ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY default_allow ON public.test AS PERMISSIVE FOR ALL TO PUBLIC USING (TRUE);
    ```

1. Try to append to this table via `DBI::dbAppendTable()`:

    ```r
    DBI::dbAppendTable(conn = DBI::dbConnect(drv = RPostgres::Postgres(), ...),
                       name = DBI::Id(schema = "public",
                                      table = "test"),
                       value = tibble::tibble(title = "First one"))
    ```

    (Complete the `conn` arg with valid credentials!)

    It will fail with the following error:

    ```
    Error: Failed to initialise COPY : ERROR:  COPY FROM not supported with row-level security
    HINT:  Use INSERT statements instead.
    ```

    Without RLS enabled, `dbAppendTable()` succeeds.

I'm unsure whether this issue should be reported here or rather over at the [DBI repo](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/). Please let me know if I should move it there.

title: dbQuoteIdentifier() does not allow columns in Id() object.
description:
`dbQuoteIdentifier()` currently does not allow for columns when quoting an `Id()` object.

    library(DBI)

    con <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "postgres")

    id <- DBI::Id(table = "table_name", column = "column_name")

    dbQuoteIdentifier(conn = con, x = id)
    #> Error in dbQuoteIdentifier(conn = con, x = id): all(names(x@name) %in% c("catalog", "schema", "table")) is not TRUE

I think it should, and the [`glue_sql()` docs](https://glue.tidyverse.org/reference/glue_sql.html) seem to agree (the last example contains an implizit `dbQuoteIdentifier()` if I am not mistaken).

    cols <- list(
      DBI::Id(table = "table_name", column = "col1"),
      DBI::Id(table = "table_name", column = "col2")
    )

    glue::glue_sql("SELECT {`cols`*}", .con = con)
    #> Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...): all(names(x@name) %in% c("catalog", "schema", "table")) is not TRUE

    dbDisconnect(con)

Would it suffice to add `"column"` here:

https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/blob/12c3d3dc67f93cbafca24b5496d2fc1a9cf0f562/R/quote.R#L58

and change

https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/blob/12c3d3dc67f93cbafca24b5496d2fc1a9cf0f562/R/quote.R#L61-L71

to

```r
return(SQL(paste0(dbQuoteIdentifier(conn, x@name), collapse = ".")))
```

(from https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/6531ab38fc0d21745b1f40fdd836ba82f926c287/R/quote.R#L112)

Or am I missing something?

title: RPostgres dbConnect crashes with segfault in R 4.2.3 running on RHEL 8
description:
We have a postgresql v14 database running on RHEL 7 server. I was able to connect to it using RPostgres 1.4.5 / R 4.2.3 from our HPC which runs on RHEL 8. Last night, we updated SSL certificates for postgresql v14 server as we were getting `ee key too small` error from an updated openssl library. [Related thread](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67754773/1243763). So, we updated SSL certificates signed using 2048 key length (instead of earlier 1024 key length). While postgresql server is running ok with new SSL and we can connect to it from R and other interfaces (pgadmin, pgweb, etc.), I get following error while connecting using RPostgres package v1.4.5 or an updated v1.4.6. This error only appears on our HPC running R 4.2.3 on RHEL 8 but not on my macbook where the same command can connect to postgres server though mac runs R 4.3.1.

```r
library(RPostgres)
```

title: Memory leak when querying from a packaged function
description:
I am connecting to a Redshift Serverless deployment using RPostgres. Let's call that connection `con`:

```R
r$> class(con)
[1] "PqConnection"
attr(,"package")
[1] "RPostgres"
```

I am trying to read a table with a where statement. In my case the result is about 144MB:
```R
r$> object.size(a)/1024/1024
144.7 bytes
```

If I run the following command:
```R
a=DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "select * from schema.table where column = 'value'")
```

a few times, I see memory usage jump sharply on the first connection (around 1.5GB), then it keeps increasing moderately as I keep rerunning that statement, until stabilizing at ~2GB total RAM.

However, if I wrap the call in a function:
```R
test_db_con=function(con){
  ret=dbGetQuery(con, "select * from schema.table where column = 'value'")
  return(ret)
}
```

and put it in a package, the following:
```R
devtools::load_all()
## create con
a=test_db_con(con=con)
```

has a different behavior. No matter how many times I run the last line, memory usage never peaks. Instead it keeps increasing, by increments larger than the size of the data (around 500MB), eventually leading to OOM. To me, this hints at a memory leak problem, but I don't know why this would happen only in a package. FWIW, I am running this on an AWS EC2 instance, and the issue also happens when using `PostgreSQL` (although the memory explosion there seems much more pronounced). Any help appreciated !

Version info:
```R
r$> DBI::dbGetInfo(RPostgres::Postgres())
$driver.version
[1] ‘1.4.6’

$client.version
[1] ‘14.10’
```

title: Polygon/multipolygon columns: incorrect write, correct read
description:
# Incorrect write

If we open a regular DBI connection, as in the next example, we won't correctly write to Postgres with Postgis correctly configured.

```
library(RPostgres)
library(sf)
library(archive)

con <- dbConnect(
  drv = Postgres(),
  dbname = "shiny"
)

download.file("https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2014/TRACT/tl_2014_01_tract.zip", "tl_2014_01_tract.zip")

archive_extract("tl_2014_01_tract.zip")

d <- read_sf("tl_2014_01_tract.shp")

# this saves geometry as text
# sf::dbWriteTable(con, "carto", d, append = TRUE)
# RPostgres::dbWriteTable(con, "carto", d, append = TRUE)

# this saves geometry as geometry (not working)
# st_write(d, con, "carto", append = TRUE, layer = "carto", layer_options = c("GEOMETRY_NAME=geometry"))

# this saves geometry as geometry
st_write(
  d2,
  "PG:host=localhost port=5432 dbname=shiny user=xxx password=yyy",
  layer = "carto",
  layer_options = c("GEOMETRY_NAME=geometry"),
  append = TRUE
)
```

# Correct read

```
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Ggplot2 won't like the <pq_gmtry> but it's correct
d2 <- tbl(con, "carto") %>%
    filter(countyfp == "001") %>%
    collect()

glimpse(d2)

# convert pq_gmtry to multipolygon
d2 <- d2 %>%
  mutate(geometry = st_as_sfc(geometry))

dbDisconnect(con)
```

I'd run into some issues with trying to upload data to redshift using RPostgres and non-Redshift-specific drivers a couple years ago and developed a workaround then that relied on pushing data to S3 first and then copying it into Redshift.

That solution utilizes the somehow-still-working RedshiftTools package, so when I was doing some refactoring, I was eager to see if DBI::dbWriteTable had made any progress on this project in the couple years since, and figured I'd toss a reprex your way with any bugs I saw.

---

It is "hard" to get data into redshift in ways that probably shouldn't be hard. Both `dplyr::copy_to()` and `dbplyr::dbWriteTable()` don't work as expected for me, and I'm forced to rely on a hackier workaround than I'd like to. 

If one outcome of this bug report is to say "You should use use `dbWriteTable()` to upload a CSV instead of DF, that's totally fine w/ me, but that part should probably be fixed to work w/ schema naming and `DBI::Id` just like the "lite" version with the small DF does. 

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dbplyr))

db <- DBI::dbConnect(
    drv      = RPostgres::Redshift(),
    host     = "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    port     = "5439",
    user     = keyring::key_get(service = "rs_un_airflow_prod"),
    password = keyring::key_get(service = "rs_pw_airflow_prod"),
    dbname   = 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx',
    sslmode  = "require"
)

db2 <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = ":memory:")

# db3 <- simulate_redshift() # Wish these worked with DBI for reprex purposes but they don't...
# db4 <- simulate_sqlite()

test_df_full <- nycflights13::flights
test_df_lite <- nycflights13::flights %>% slice(1:100)
    
temp_path_full <- tempfile()
temp_path_lite <- tempfile()

db_path_full_rs <- DBI::Id(schema = 'public', table = 'test_df_full')
db_path_lite_rs <- DBI::Id(schema = 'public', table = 'test_df_lite')
db_path_full_sq <- DBI::Id(schema = NULL, table = 'test_df_full')
db_path_lite_sq <- DBI::Id(schema = NULL, table = 'test_df_lite')

readr::write_csv(x = test_df_full, file = temp_path_full)
readr::write_csv(x = test_df_full, file = temp_path_lite)

# Writing with the df itself only works for small enough DFs in Redshift
DBI::dbWriteTable(conn = db, name = db_path_full_rs, value = test_df_full, overwrite = T)
#> Error: Failed to prepare query: ERROR:  Statement is too large. Statement Size: 77989149 bytes. Maximum Allowed: 16777216 bytes
DBI::dbWriteTable(conn = db, name = db_path_lite_rs, value = test_df_lite, overwrite = T)

db %>% tbl(db_path_full_rs) %>% tally() # Expected: n = 336,776; Actual: Error
#> Error in `db_query_fields.DBIConnection()`:
#> ! Can't query fields.
#> Caused by error:

db %>% tbl(db_path_lite_rs) %>% tally() # Expected: n = 100; Actual: n = 100
#> # Source:   SQL [1 x 1]
#> # Database: postgres  [kunal_ha@airflow-production-redshift.data.crickethealth.com:5439/eff_swh]

# Both work in SQLite and Microsoft SQL though
DBI::dbWriteTable(conn = db2, name = db_path_full_sq, value = test_df_full, overwrite = T)
```

title: Redshift Scientific Notation Triggers Incorrect Multiple Queries Error
description:
Since updating from RPostgres 1.3.3 to 1.4.3, I'm getting this error on one of my Redshift queries when I don't expect: `Error: Multiple queries must use the same column types.` 

It seems to be related to using scientific notation in a very specific circumstance around filling NULLs after a window function.

```r
# open connection
conn <- RPostgres::dbConnect(RPostgres::Redshift()
                             , host =
                             , port = 
                             , user = 
                             , password = 
                             , dbname = )

query_BROKEN <- '
select coalesce(lead(num) over (order by num), 1e10)
from (
  select 1 as num
  union all
  select 2 as num
  union all
  select 3 as num
)
'

query_WORKS <- '
select coalesce(lead(num) over (order by num), 10000000)
from (
  select 1 as num
  union all
  select 2 as num
  union all
  select 3 as num
)
'

print(RPostgres::dbGetQuery(conn, query_WORKS))
# coalesce
# 1        2
# 2        3
# 3 10000000

print(RPostgres::dbGetQuery(conn, query_BROKEN))
# Error: Multiple queries must use the same column types.

RPostgres::dbDisconnect(conn)
```

title: Printing of "invalid" `PqConnection` object
description:
For unit testing purposes, I'm trying to create a dummy `PqConnection` object. One minor inconvenience is that while `format.PqConnection()` checks for validity and handles the "invalid" case gracefully, `show_PqConnection()` does not. 

---

Therefore printing an object created as `new("PqConnection")` will trigger an error:

```r
library(RPostgres)
dummy <- new("PqConnection")
format(dummy)
#> [1] "<PqConnection> DISCONNECTED"
dummy
#> Error: Invalid connection
```

Is there a reason for not calling `format()` internally in `show_PqConnection()`? Happy to submit a PR if you're open to the idea.

title: Something wrong with the 1.4.5 Mac binary on CRAN with Redshift
description:
I discovered an odd issue, which I thought I'd report and can help troubleshoot if needed. The tl;dr is that I cannot connect to one Redshift server with the Mac binary from CRAN, but can if I compile from source.

The current Mac binary of `RPostgres` (1.4.5) seems to have an issue with some, but not all, Redshift servers. The command I'm running is
```
DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Redshift(), ...) # same result with RPostgres::Postgres()
```
and the error I get is:

```
connection to server at "<host>" (<ip>), port 5439 failed: server closed the connection unexpectedly
	This probably means the server terminated abnormally
	before or while processing the request.
```

The error message is the same also when I don't provide a valid username/password, so it seems to happen before authentication.

The weird thing is that I get this error with only one Redshift server (our production one) and not with another (our staging) – even though they're both running the same version. Also, I can connect to both with `psql` from my Mac, and can connect to both with `RPostgres` from within a docker container running on my Mac. This made me suspect it is somehow related to the Mac version of `RPostgres`. And in fact, if instead of installing the binary from CRAN I compile it from source with (I have `libpq` installed with Homebrew):
```
install.packages("RPostgres", type = "source")
```

The problem goes away and I can connect to both servers.

I don't know if the solution is to simply recompile the Mac binary version that is available on CRAN, and that will fix it. If not, I can help troubleshoot on my end, in case that helps. title: dbGetQuery failing due to stale Redshift OIDs
description:
# Overview

I am querying an AWS Redshift table over an `RPostgres::Redshift` connection. The query sometimes fails with error:

```
Error: Failed to fetch row: ERROR:  could not open relation with OID 8574286
```

The `ERROR:  could not open relation with OID <oid-number>` portion of the error comes from Redshift and the OID is different each time.

## Environment

The `RPostgres::Redshift` connection is running on an Ubuntu 20.04 machine with libpq-dev 12.19-0ubuntu0.20.04.1, R 4.2.1, DBI 1.2.3, and RPostgres 1.4.5.

# Description

The table in question is managed by an independent process which replaces the table periodically. The table OID changes each time it is replaced. When the table replacement process executes, it drops the table and renames a replacement table in a single transaction:

```sql
BEGIN TRANSACTION;

DROP TABLE my_table;
ALTER TABLE my_table_tmp RENAME TO my_table;

END TRANSACTION;
```

When a query over a `RPostgres::Redshift` connection occurs at the same time, the above error is returned.

```r
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT col1, col2 FROM my_table")
```

I suspect that the select statement is not creating a lock on `my_table`, which is allowing the table replacement to happen concurrently. This changes the table OID and the select query fails trying to find a stale OID.

My expectation is that the query would run without error, possibly a bit slower if it has to wait for the table replacement to complete.

title: Curious bug with transaction and `dbSendQuery()`
description:
I'm not sure if this is expected behaviour, a bug in RPostgres, or a bug in Postgres itself. But it took quite some time to figure out the issue...

``` r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())

write_table <- function(n) {
  DBI::dbWriteTable(
    con,
    "df_x",
    tibble::tibble(x = 1:n),
    temporary = TRUE,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}


DBI::dbWithTransaction(
  con, {
    write_table(2e3)
    res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM df_x")
    DBI::dbFetch(res, n = 0)
    DBI::dbClearResult(res)
    DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM df_x LIMIT 1")
  }
)
#> Error: Failed to prepare query: ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block

# Interestingly, this works if the table is small
DBI::dbWithTransaction(
  con, {
    write_table(200)
    res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM df_x")
    DBI::dbFetch(res, n = 0)
    DBI::dbClearResult(res)
    DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM df_x LIMIT 1")
  }
)
#>   x
#> 1 1
```

title: Failure to acquire connections on Mac OS within multicore fork()-ed process
description:
After a recent upgrade to R 4.2.2, DBI 1.1.3, RPostgres 1.4.4, and PostgreSQL 14.6, I find I can't acquire DB connections from within a forked multicore process **when specifying the host**. To be clear, I'm _not_ trying to share connections across processes; here's a reprex: ```R library(parallel) mclapply(1:2, function(i) { conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), host = "localhost", dbname = "mydb") try(DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)) }, mc.cores = 2) ``` If the `host` argument is left _completely_ unspecified (this includes not being present in any PostgreSQL service file, as described below), connections are made correctly. Failures occur in a variety of other scenarios I've tested: * When `host = "localhost"` is replaced with `host = "127.0.01"`. * When `host` is omitted in favor of the (better, IMO) libpq "service" mechanism with a `.pg_service.conf` file, i.e. where the connection call looks like so: `DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), service = "myservice")`, and the service file contains the host spec. * When the host is either local ("localhost") or remote. In all scenarios above, the errors looks like so: ``` objc[55661]: +[__NSPlaceholderDate initialize] may have been in progress in another thread when fork() was called. objc[55661]: +[__NSPlaceholderDate initialize] may have been in progress in another thread when fork() was called. We cannot safely call it or ignore it in the fork() child process. Crashing instead. Set a breakpoint on objc_initializeAfterForkError to debug. objc[55660]: +[__NSPlaceholderDate initialize] may have been in progress in another thread when fork() was called. objc[55660]: +[__NSPlaceholderDate initialize] may have been in progress in another thread when fork() was called. We cannot safely call it or ignore it in the fork() child process. Crashing instead. Set a breakpoint on objc_initializeAfterForkError to debug. ``` This is unique to the multicore case, as setting `mc.cores = 1` while also leaving the `host` parameter in the connection call also works fine (i.e. without error). My OS version (11.3, "Big Sur") was not part of the upgrade cycle. I did re-install DBI & RPostgres (from source) after the R version upgrade (was previously on 4.0.3), and I've even re-installed PostgreSQL, _then_ re-installed RPostgres to try to make sure all binaries being built were linking against the correct libraries. A workaround I've found has been to initiate the R session (and thus the sub-processes) with this environment variable & value: ``` OBJC_DISABLE_INITIALIZE_FORK_SAFETY=YES ``` However, I'm wary of this 'solution' and am wondering if anyone else has run into this issues with DBI & RPostgres while specifying the `host` parameter of the connection call. (Removing that parameter isn't ideal for my use case, as it's typically interpolated from a CLI arg.)

title: Redshift varchar character length not respected by dplyr::rows_*()
description:
I first created [this issue in the dbplyr repo](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/issues/1050) but their suggestion is that it's an RPosgres issue.

I hope this is the right place for this issue. I know that dplyr::rows_*() are experimental.

When writing a text value to a Redshift table whose column is varchar(anything larger than 256), using dplyr::rows_append() or dplyr::rows_update() seems to cast the text to varchar(256) before writing to the database. Longer texts will then fail to write even though the table should be able to accommodate them.

To reproduce the issue:
- Create a Redshift table with columns id and txt (I haven't run into this with Postgres connections but it might happen there too).
- Make the datatype of the txt column varchar(max, or anything larger than 256)
- Connect to the table using a privileged user. I use RPostgres::Redshift() (but this isn't the issue).
- This will work successfully.
```r
dplyr::rows_append(x = dplyr::tbl(src = redshift_conn, DBI::Id(schema = schema, table = table)), y = tibble(id = 1, txt = paste(rep('a', 256), collapse = '')), copy = TRUE, in_place = TRUE)
```
- This will fail with `Error: Failed to fetch row: ERROR:  value too long for type character varying(256).`
```r
dplyr::rows_append(x = dplyr::tbl(src = redshift_conn, DBI::Id(schema = schema, table = table)), y = tibble(id = 2, txt = paste(rep('a', 257), collapse = '')), copy = TRUE, in_place = TRUE)
```
- But using RPostgres::dbAppendTable() works with the same data that failed with dplyr::rows_append().
```r
RPostgres::dbAppendTable(conn = redshift_conn, name = DBI::Id(schema = schema, table = table), value = tibble(id = 2, txt = paste(rep('a', 257), collapse = '')), row.names = NULL)
```

Somewhere along the line the text value is cast from varchar(65535) to varchar(256) for rows_append() and rows_update(), and I haven't figured out where.

Thanks!

title: RPostgres should respect system timezone rather than default to UTC
description:
When connecting to a Postgres backend server, RPostgres sets the timezone for the connection to UTC by default (see for example #222). This is odd behaviour, as virtually any other database abstraction system defaults to either not setting the time zone and thus using the Postgres backend server timezone OR defaulting to using the user's system time zone. 

The consequence of setting `timezone="UTC"` by default leads to unexpected behaviour (not wrong behaviour, just unexpected). A better option to me seems to default to the user's system time zone. This should not be hard to implement (although systems might differ in how they store TZ information, e.g. environmental variable `TZ` or in `/etc/timezone`.

...unless I'm simply overlooking something and UTC is actually appropriate.

title: Revisit EINTR handling with check_interrupts = TRUE
`dbListObjects()` does not list empty schemata
description:
`dbListObjects()` does not list empty schemata, i.e. a schema without a table.

``` r
library(RPostgres)
con <- postgresDefault()
dbExecute(con, paste0('CREATE SCHEMA "Robert"'))
#> [1] 0
dbListObjects(con)
#>                              table is_prefix
#> 1 <Id> schema = information_schema      TRUE
#> 2         <Id> schema = pg_catalog      TRUE
```

The schema is listed in `information_schema.schemata` or `pg_catalog.pg_namespace` (the (empty) `public` schema is also not listed by `dbListObjects()` BTW)

``` r
dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata;')
#>          schema_name
#> 1           pg_toast
#> 2         pg_catalog
#> 3             public
#> 4 information_schema
#> 5             Robert
dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT * FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace;')
#>     oid            nspname nspowner                              nspacl
#> 1    99           pg_toast       10                                <NA>
#> 2    11         pg_catalog       10  {postgres=UC/postgres,=U/postgres}
#> 3  2200             public       10 {postgres=UC/postgres,=UC/postgres}
#> 4 13111 information_schema       10  {postgres=UC/postgres,=U/postgres}
#> 5 16417             Robert       10                                <NA>
```

The schema is also listed by `dbListObjects()` after adding a table

``` r
table_qid <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, Id(schema = 'Robert', table = "mtcars"))
dbWriteTable(con, table_qid, mtcars)
dbListObjects(con)
#>                              table is_prefix
#> 1 <Id> schema = information_schema      TRUE
#> 2             <Id> schema = Robert      TRUE
#> 3         <Id> schema = pg_catalog      TRUE

# clean-up
dbExecute(con, paste0('DROP TABLE ', table_qid))
#> [1] 0
dbExecute(con, paste0('DROP SCHEMA "Robert"'))
#> [1] 0
dbDisconnect(con)
```

The reason for this is that `dbListObjects()` [uses `information_schema.tables`](https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/blob/a1bd3b61425886b207462a24d63a86fdd99a1f19/R/dbListObjects_PqConnection_ANY.R#L16-L19) to look up tables and schemata, but naturally the `information_schema.tables` view does not list schemata if they do not contain a table.

title: `dbQuoteLiteral()` should return typed `NULL`
description:
Currently, `dbQuoteLiteral()` simply returns `NULL` for missing values

```r
DBI::dbQuoteLiteral(con, c(1L, NA_integer_))
#> <SQL> 1::int4
#> <SQL> NULL
```

While this is usually okay, this doesn't work well when creating a table via a values clause

```r
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
r"{WITH tbl1 AS (
 SELECT NULL AS "country", NULL AS "date" WHERE false
), tbl2 AS (
  SELECT NULL AS "country", NULL AS "date" WHERE false
  UNION ALL
  VALUES
    ('de', '2021-11-19'::date)
)
SELECT tbl1.*
FROM tbl1
INNER JOIN tbl2
ON (tbl1.country = tbl2.country AND tbl1.date = tbl2.date)}"
)

#> Error: Failed to prepare query: ERROR:  operator does not exist: text = date
#> LINE 15: ON (tbl1.country = tbl2.country, tbl1.date = tbl2.date)
```

With a typed `NULL` this works nicely

```r
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
r"{WITH tbl1 AS (
 SELECT NULL::text AS "country", NULL::date AS "date" WHERE false
), tbl2 AS (
  SELECT NULL AS "country", NULL AS "date" WHERE false
  UNION ALL
  VALUES
    ('de', '2021-11-19'::date)
)
SELECT tbl1.*
FROM tbl1
INNER JOIN tbl2
ON (tbl1.country = tbl2.country AND tbl1.date = tbl2.date)}"
)
```

This is an issue for the `db_values()` function which hopefully soon comes to `dbplyr` (see https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/pull/678)

title: dbQuoteLiteral() can't handle zero-length **typed** values
description:
When passed a typed, length-zero vector, {RPostgres}' `dbQuoteIdentifier()` method yields a length-one string that triggers a Postgres SQL syntax error. The `ANSI()` driver behaves differently (and, I think, correctly).
```r
## db_conn is my RPostgres connection

str(DBI::dbQuoteLiteral(DBI::ANSI(), integer(0)))
# Formal class 'SQL' [package "DBI"] with 1 slot
#   ..@ .Data: chr(0)

str(DBI::dbQuoteLiteral(db_conn, integer(0)))
# Formal class 'SQL' [package "DBI"] with 1 slot
#  ..@ .Data: chr "::int4"
```
Injecting the RPostgres value into a query, e.g. via `glue::glue_sql()` yields something like so:
```r
my_val <- DBI::dbQuoteLiteral(db_conn, integer(0))
sql <- glue::glue_sql("select * from my_tbl where {my_val}", .con = db_conn)
DBI::dbGetQuery(db_conn, sql)
#  Error: Failed to prepare query: ERROR:  syntax error at or near "::"
#  LINE 1: select * from my_tbl where ::int4
```
FWIW, `NULL` as an input across both `ANSI()` and RPostgres connections/drivers works fine, this error is _specifically_ in the length-zero **typed** case.

{RPostgres} v1.2.1
{DBI} v1.1.0

title: Error: Failed to fetch row: ERROR: SET datestyle takes only one argument.
description:
---
First, and most importantly, I send my sincere thanks for the work you do maintaining this important R library. 

I am having an issue using RPostgres to connect to CockroachDB. When I attempt to connect, R returns an error:

I posted my issue on Cockroach's forum. I appreciate your assistance with this.

```r
con = dbConnect(dbDriver("Postgres"),
                dbname = "MyDatabase", 
                host = "free-tier4.aws-us-west-2.cockroachlabs.cloud", 
                port = '26257',

                )
```

title: Dates not casting within intervals
description:
When filtering by date ranges, date values are not cast properly so `dbplyr` doesn't form proper queries.

---

Brief description of the problem

```r
library(DBI)
library(tibble)
library(RPostgres)
# use whatever Postgres connection you have
con <- postgresDefault()

init_data <- tibble(
  x = Sys.Date()-1:10
)

dbWriteTable(con, "test_table", init_data)

test_table <- tbl(con, "test_table")
# filter with date interval
test_table %>% filter(
  x > !!Sys.Date() - weeks(1)
)
# errors: invalid input syntax for type interval: "2021-11-28"
test_table %>% filter(
  x > !!Sys.Date() - weeks(1)
) %>% show_query()
# SELECT *
# FROM `test_table`
# WHERE (`x` > '2021-11-30' - weeks(1.0))
### should be
# SELECT *
#   FROM `test_table`
# WHERE (`x` > '2021-11-30'::date - weeks(1.0))
```
Apologies if this issue should be elsewhere in `DBI` ecosystem

title: Installation on Centos8
description:
An error occurred when I tried to install RPostgres package on Centos8 with postgresql-13 : 
-lpq -L/usr/lib64/R/lib -lR
/usr/bin/ld : ne peut trouver -lpq
collect2: error: ld a retourné le statut de sortie 1
make: *** [/usr/share/R/make/shlib.mk:10: RPostgres.so] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘RPostgres’

This error was due to default path and environment variables given by postgresql-13. The LIB_DIR wasn't set and the documentation of installation doesn't mention how to set it. I either didn't find any bug report for that problem. 

I correct that problem by modifying the configure shell to get the PKG_LIBS environment variable from the calling shell. 
But I guess that a cleaner solution consist to set the LIB_DIR environment variable (and export it) to the library installation directory (/usr/pgsql-13/lib/ by default). This solution would be reduced to a documentation mention. 

Hope this help

The set-up to replicate this issue is a bit involved but docker helps

Start a postgres docker container setting a password to `foo`

```
docker run --rm --name postgres -e "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=foo" -p 5432:5432 postgres
```

Start a second container with `pgbouncer` acting as a per-transaction connection pooler (the same thing occurs with per-statement pooling, but using `pool_mode=session` works just fine it seems)

```
docker run --rm --name pgbouncer --link postgres:postgres -e "POSTGRES_ENV_PASSWORD=foo" -e "pool_mode=transaction" -p 6432:6432 kafka/pgbouncer
```

```
psql -h localhost -p 6432 -U postgres -c \\dt
```

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
```

title: per-query bigint option
description:
Kirill, I'm finally catching up on the `RPostgres` version, thanks for your efforts on this.

I'm confident that the switch to `bit64::integer64` as the default was not made hastily, and I'm glad we have the capability. Since there are many aspects of base R that deal silently-incorrectly with this type, has there been discussion on being able to switch the `bigint=` argument per-query or even per-column?

**Use Case**: pre-existing processes that may rely on significant external code that either have unknown or known-bad compatibility with `bit64::integer64`, but with a connection where 64-bit numbers are needed for some fields. Setting it in `dbConnect` would still be relevant (as the default), but it'd be nice to be able to still use 64-bits when needed.

```r
con <- dbConnect(..., bigint="integer")
dbGetQuery(con, "select 1 as a") # uses the dbConnect option
dbGetQuery(con, "select 1 as a", bigint="integer64") # overrides
```

It's likely going too far, but would anyone see utility in doing it per-column? The workaround until then would be to split the query into two, but this has the potential of being rather inefficient SQL-wise.

```r
dbGetQuery(con, "select 1 as isbig, 2 as isnotbig", bigint=c(isbig="integer64",isnotbig="integer"))
```

where the code might be:

```r
convert_bigint_fields <- function (conn, ret, bigint = conn@bigint) {
    bignms <- names(bigint)
    if (is.null(bignms)) {
      bigint <- setNames(rep(bigint, ncol(ret)), colnames(ret))
    }
    # set all others as default
    bigint[ setdiff(colnames(ret), names(bigint)) ] <- 'default'
    # reorder them
    bigint <- bigint[colnames(ret)]
    is_int64 <- vlapply(ret, inherits, "integer64")
    funs <- list(integer = as.integer, numeric = as.numeric, character = as.character)
    for (funnm in names(funs)) {
      istype <- is_int64 & (bigint == funnm)
      ret[istype] <- lapply(ret[istype], funs[[funnm]])
    }
    ret
}
```

Same on macOS and Linux. Not tested on Windows.

``` r
session <- callr::r_session$new()

session$run(function() {
  library(RPostgres)
  .GlobalEnv$conn <- dbConnect(Postgres(), check_interrupts = TRUE)
  invisible()
})
#> NULL
session$call(function() {
  tryCatch(
    print(dbGetQuery(.GlobalEnv$conn, "SELECT pg_sleep(2)")),
    error = identity
  )
})

session$poll_process(100)
```

title: Confusing error for names in parameterized queries
description:
This is perhaps related to #199 but hopefully a simpler request.

Presently this code...

```r
dat <- data.frame(foo = 1:3, bar = 4:6)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "INSERT INTO sometable (foo, bar) VALUES ($1, $2);")
dbBind(rs, params = dat)
dbClearResults(rs)
```
...provokes an error: 'Named parameters not supported'.

This confused me because the code has positional rather than named placeholders. After looking at the package sources (PgResult.R line 172) I arrived at this work-around:

```r
dbBind(rs, params = unname(dat))
```

Would it cause problems if names were just ignored rather than raising an error? If so, perhaps adding an example of this work-around to the docs would help others.

title: RPostgres on Mac fails to connect to Amazon RDS Aurora database
description:
One of our Postgres databases was recently migrated to an AWS Aurora RDS instance. Since then, any attempt to connect to the DB:

`conn <- DBI::dbConnect(
  drv = RPostgres::Postgres(),
  dbname = 'xxx',
  host = 'xxx',
  port = 5432,
  user = 'xxx',
  password = 'xxx')`

is rejected with the following message:

`Error: server closed the connection unexpectedly
        This probably means the server terminated abnormally
        before or while processing the request.` 

The problem is reproducible across several machines running OSX (10.15.7) but the connection is established fine when running from Centos7 and Windows 10. All environments running R (4.0.4), DBI (1.1.1), RPostgres (1.3.2), and Rcpp (1.0.6).

Replacing the driver specification by RPostgreSQL::PostgreSQL() solves the issue which is what lead me to open this issue.

title: check_interrupts = TRUE causes certain query with inner join to fail with error message "select() on the connection failed"
description:
The following query, when run through `dbGetQuery()` fails when using `check_interupts = TRUE` in `dbConnect()`. Error message is "select() on the connection failed"

```SQL
select dsc.dw_customer_key
from dws_customer dsc
inner join tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019 tmp 
  on tmp.dw_customer_key = dsc.dw_customer_key
where 1 = 1 and dsc.dw_distribution_key between 201902 * 1337 and 201903 * 1337
limit 10
```

The queries are run against my company's Data warehouse. 

Queries including only one of the tables `dws_customer` or `tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019` work. Queries with other inner joins work fine.

```r
bad_query <- "select dsc.dw_customer_key
from dws_customer dsc
inner join tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019 tmp 
  on tmp.dw_customer_key = dsc.dw_customer_key
where 1 = 1 and dsc.dw_distribution_key between 201902 * 1337 and 201903 * 1337
limit 10"

# Shows that we can fetch from dws_customer
working_query <- "select dsc.dw_customer_key 
from dws_customer dsc 
limit 10"

# Shows that we can fetch from tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019
working_query2 <- "select tmp.dw_customer_key
from tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019 tmp
limit 10"

# shows that we can do inner joins 
working_query3 <- "select 
  dfc.dw_contact_event_key, 
  ddc.external_info1_description
from dwf_contact dfc
inner join dwd_contact_event ddc 
    on ddc.dw_contact_event_key = dfc.dw_contact_event_key
limit 10"

library(DBI)

# Following fails on last query
tmp_con <- 
  dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
            dbname = "dw_db",
            host = "company DW", 
            port = "proper port", 
            user = "foobar", 
            password = "foobar",
            check_interrupts = TRUE)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con, working_query)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con, working_query2)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con, working_query3)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con, bad_query) # Error: select() on the connection failed
dbDisconnect(tmp_con)
```

Changing the order in which queries are run, doesn't change the result. 

If we set `check_interrupts = FALSE` the query works. The others work as well.

```r
# Following works
tmp_con2 <- 
  dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
            dbname = "dw_db",
            host = "company DW", 
            port = "proper port", 
            user = "foobar", 
            password = "foobar",
            check_interrupts = FALSE)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con2, working_query)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con2, working_query2)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con2, working_query3)
dbGetQuery(tmp_con2, bad_query)
dbDisconnect(tmp_con2)
```

All four queries work under RPostgreSQL as well.

**EDIT:**

Having done a bit more investigation, I have found some more bugs/weird behaviour.

If I remove the condition in `bad_query` it runs fine. Some times `working_query` also fails with `"Error: select() on the connection failed"` when it is run as the first query of an open connection, but not all the time. 

The two tables `dws_customer` and `tmp_20200420_customer_reg_dates_2019` lie in two different schemas, but this doesn't seem to be the culprit, as I am able to join other tables from the two schemas. 

The error also appears with `check_interrupts = TRUE` when I construct a query that returns 0 rows. Using `check_interrupts = FALSE` I get a data.frame of 0 rows with the appropriate columns.

title: Timestamp without time zone problem
description:
I have a database with a column of type "timestamp without time zone".
    
Times reported by that column are converted to the local timezone by RPostgres even though the server runs UTC.
    
Here's an example:
    
```{r}
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
    
print.default(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT CAST('2010-06-01 00:00:00' AS timestamp) AS timestamp")$timestamp)
#> [1] 1275343200
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
    
print.default(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT extract(epoch from CAST('2010-06-01 00:00:00' AS timestamp)) as epoch")$epoch)
#> [1] 1275350400
```
The last value is the correct epoch for 2010-06-01 00:00:00 UTC.

I think the problem is related to `as.POSIXct` having `tz=""` as default, ie converting using the local timezone, but RPostgres uses "UTC" in the connection by default.
    
At least this shows the same:
    
```{r}
print.default(as.POSIXct("2010-06-01 00:00:00"))
#> [1] 1275343200
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
#> attr(,"tzone")
#> [1] ""

print.default(as.POSIXct("2010-06-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC"))
#> [1] 1275350400
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
#> attr(,"tzone")
#> [1] "UTC"
```
    
I suggest RPostgres should use `as.POSIXct()` with `tz="UTC"` (actually the value of `timezone` in dbConnect) when converting values from a column of type "timestamp without time zone".

The problem goes away if timestamp with time zone is used:

```
print.default(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT CAST('2010-06-01 00:00:00' AS timestamp with time zone) AS timestamp")$timestamp)
#> [1] 1275350400
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
```

title: Incorrect results when aggregating timestamp to date
description:
There seems to be a problem with RPostgres when retrieving results involving aggregating `timestamp with time zone` columns to date. The SQL that is generated (displayed with `show_query()`) yields a different result than what is actually retrieved by RPostgres. RPostgreSQL generates the same SQL, and retrieves the correct result.

In the following example, focus on the 2019-05-01 data, which should have a minimum of 24 and a maximum of 47.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(RPostgres)

conn <- dbConnect(Postgres(),
                  host = "dbhost",
                  user = "dbuser",
                  dbname = "dbname")

example <- tibble(val = seq(0:70)) %>%
    mutate(ts = ymd_hms("2019-04-30 00:00:00", tz = "US/Alaska") + hours(val))

example %>%
    mutate(dte = date(ts)) %>%
    group_by(dte) %>%
    summarize(min = min(val, na.rm = TRUE),
              max = max(val, na.rm = TRUE))
```

That yields the correct result:

```
  dte          min   max
  <date>     <int> <int>
1 2019-04-30     1    23
2 2019-05-01    24    47
3 2019-05-02    48    71
```

If we round-trip this through the database we get a different answer:

```{r}
dbWriteTable(conn, "example", example,
             overwrite = TRUE, append = FALSE)

conn %>%
    tbl("example") %>%
    mutate(dte = date(ts)) %>%
    group_by(dte) %>%
    summarize(min = min(val, na.rm = TRUE),
              max = max(val, na.rm = TRUE))
```

Here's the result. The values for min and max appear to be off by 8 hours as though it's treating the timestamp of the data in the database as UTC (rather than US/Alaska).

```
  dte          min   max
  <date>     <int> <int>
1 2019-04-30     1    15
2 2019-05-02    40    63
3 2019-05-03    64    71
4 2019-05-01    16    39
```

It's not the query that is generated, which gives the correct result when run inside Postgres. I get the same query when I load RPostgreSQL and use it's database driver, but it loads the proper results.

Here's the `show_query()` output:

```
<SQL>
SELECT "dte", MIN("val") AS "min", MAX("val") AS "max"
FROM (SELECT "val", "ts", date("ts") AS "dte"
FROM "example") "dbplyr_057"
GROUP BY "dte"
```

And the results of that query when run inside the database using `psql`:

```
    dte     | min | max
------------+-----+-----
 2019-04-30 |   1 |  23
 2019-05-01 |  24 |  47
 2019-05-02 |  48 |  71
```

title: dbGetQuery assuming postgres database is in UTC?
description:
Using Rpostgres, my R session defaults to "America/Toronto" timezone, and the Postgres database I am working with is in UTC-04 by default. I'm finding that even if I change the session time zone in Postgres to "localtime" (which helps WHERE statements work correctly), dbGetQuery() still shifts the time down four hours when displaying it in R. 

Does dbGetQuery() and company just always assume the Postgres database is 'UTC' no matter what the actual Postgres session time zone is set to? 

I noticed a fix on another manifestation of dbConnect() in the odbc world [here](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/commit/fcba5dc96d5aeee06695183b391d8cdf6320dc40#diff-ea07e821ea0259e09f1a87f93ab1d831), so I wondered if it was a universal issue related to the generic method. 

Here is an example: 

```
library(Rpostgres)
con_pg <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())

#default R session time zone
Sys.timezone()
#> [1] "America/Toronto"


#some fake dates (one without and one with time zone)
dbExecute(con_pg, "DROP table IF EXISTS development.test")
#> [1] 0

dbExecute(
  con_pg,
  "CREATE TABLE development.test
  (
  ts_naked timestamp without time zone,
  ts_tz timestamp with time zone
  );"
)
#> [1] 0

dbExecute(con_pg, 
"INSERT INTO
development.test (ts_naked, ts_tz)
VALUES
(TIMESTAMP '2016-08-12 10:00:00-04',
  TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE '2016-08-12 10:00:00-04')")
#> [1] 1

#So weird 
dbGetQuery(con_pg, "select * from development.test WHERE ts_naked = ts_tz")
#> [1] ts_naked ts_tz   
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

#R seems to shift UP the time in Postgres 
#even though data isn't being passed between the two systems
dbGetQuery(con_pg, "select * from development.test WHERE ts_naked = ts_tz - interval '4h'")
#>              ts_naked               ts_tz
#> 1 2016-08-12 10:00:00 2016-08-12 10:00:00

#set postgres session timezone to local time (as seen in earlier issues)
dbExecute(con_pg, "set timezone to 'localtime'")
#> [1] 0

dbGetQuery(con_pg, "show timezone")
#>    TimeZone
#> 1 localtime

#The WHERE statement now works even though the ts_tz is displayed as four hours earlier by R
dbGetQuery(con_pg, "select * from development.test WHERE ts_naked = ts_tz")
#>              ts_naked               ts_tz
#> 1 2016-08-12 10:00:00 2016-08-12 06:00:00

#Setting the R session environment to UTC seems to fix it
Sys.setenv(TZ="UTC")

dbGetQuery(con_pg, "select * from development.test WHERE ts_naked = ts_tz")
#>              ts_naked               ts_tz
#> 1 2016-08-12 10:00:00 2016-08-12 10:00:00

dbGetQuery(con_pg, "select EXTRACT(TIMEZONE from ts_tz) from development.test")
#>   date_part
#> 1    -14400
```

title: Different results on Windows and Mac with timestamp columns
description:
Hi, I'm seeing inconsistencies with how `timestamp without time zone` columns behave on Mac and Windows when `Sys.getenv("TZ")` is different than `Sys.timezone()`. Tested on version 1.1.1.

Here's a minimal script to reproduce:

```r
library(DBI)

print(Sys.timezone()) # America/Los_Angeles
Sys.setenv(TZ="America/New_York") # another time zone

db <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname="rpostgres_test")

dbExecute(db, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS events")
dbExecute(db, "CREATE TABLE events (created_at TIMESTAMP)")
dbExecute(db, "INSERT INTO events VALUES ('2018-01-01 12:30:00')")

rs <- dbSendQuery(db, "SELECT * FROM events")
records <- dbFetch(rs)
print(records$created_at)
```

- On Mac (as well as with RPostgreSQL), this produces `2018-01-01 12:30:00 EST`.
- On Windows, the same code produces `2018-01-01 3:30:00 EST` (when `Sys.timezone()` is `America/Los_Angeles`). 

What seems to be happening is on Mac, `2018-01-01 12:30:00` in the database is read in the `TZ` time zone. On Windows, `2018-01-01 12:30:00` in the database is read in the `Sys.timezone()` time zone, then converted to the `TZ` time zone for display.

title: [feature request] - dbWritetable from local/remote file
Connection segfault in environment's finalizer
description:
This is a bit of a strange issue related to finalized/destroyer timing I think? I've found that if a connection is assigned to an environment and is referenced in that environment's finalizer, when the garbage collector runs the connection reference leads to a segfault. But, it _only_ leads to a segfault if the connection is assigned to the environment _after_ the finalizer has been established.

When using the `RPostgreSQL` or `SQLite` drivers, both versions of the following code examples work fine. With the `RPostgres` driver, however, only the first example works, while the second segfaults.
(Note that I can't easily use `reprex` due to the segfault :-/)

### Working case:

An environment `env` is created, two connections are assigned to `env`, then a finalizer is registered on `env`.

```R
env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
env$conn1 <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), ...) ## conn1 params here
env$conn2 <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), ...) ## conn2 params here
reg.finalizer(env, function(env) {
    lapply(unique(as.list(env)), function(x) {
        show(x)
        ##if(inherits(x, "DBIConnection")) try(DBI::dbDisconnect(x))
    })
})

rm(env)
gc()
```
And the (working; redacted) output:
```
 <PqConnection> dbname@host:5432
 <PqConnection> dbname@host:5432
          used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) max used (Mb)
 Ncells 517059 27.7     940480 50.3   716069 38.3
 Vcells 937311  7.2    1893692 14.5  1272802  9.8
```

### Segfault case:

Here an environment `env` is created, the finalizer is registered, _then_ the two connections are assigned to `env`. In the working case, the connections are assigned first, followed by the finalizer registration.

```R
env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
reg.finalizer(env, function(env) {
    lapply(unique(as.list(env)), function(x) {
        show(x)
        ##if(inherits(x, "DBIConnection")) try(DBI::dbDisconnect(x))
    })
})
env$conn1 <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), ...) ## conn1 params here
env$conn2 <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), ...) ## conn2 params here

rm(env)
gc()
```
And an example of a segfault output when `gc()` is called:
```
  *** caught segfault ***
 address 0x128, cause 'memory not mapped'

 Traceback:
  1: .Call(`_RPostgres_connection_info`, con)
  2: connection_info(dbObj@ptr)
  3: dbGetInfo(object)
  4: dbGetInfo(object)
  5: show(x)
  6: show(x)
  7: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
  8: lapply(unique(as.list(env)), function(x) {    show(x)})
  9: (function (env) {    lapply(unique(as.list(env)), function(x) {        show(x)    })})(<environment>)
```

### Other notes

In the code examples above, I'm using `show(x)` just to keep it simple. In a true working example, `show(x)` is replaced by:
```R
if(inherits(x, "DBIConnection")) try(DBI::dbDisconnect(x))
```
... to try to nicely clean-up any lingering DBI connections that I might've forgotten to close explicitly.

title: fix_posixt() formats timestamps to ambiguous timezone
description:
fix_posixt() calls format_keep_na(col, usetz = T) which in terms calls base::format(...) to format POSIXt columns. However, the formatted time could contain ambiguous timezone and result in wrong time when parsed by PostgreSQL.

For example:

2020-09-01 12:00:00 Asia/Shanghai is formatted to: "2020-09-01 12:00:00 CST", which will be parsed by PostgreSQL as Central Standard Time (North America), a 14-hour difference.

Possible solution:

I suggest calling format(t, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS%z") to format timestamps to ISO-8061 to avoid such problems.

```r
t <- lubridate::as_datetime("2020-09-01 12:00:00", tz = "Asia/Shanghai")
# "2020-09-01 12:00:00 CST" ambiguous! will be parsed as Central Standard Time by PostgreSQL
format(t, usetz = TRUE)
# "2020-09-01T12:00:00+0800" not ambiguous, will be correctly parsed
format(t, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS%z")
```

title: materialized views in dbListTables()
description:
Should Materialized Views be listed by `dbListTables()`? 

I'd argue they should since they are objects that share characteristics of both Tables and Views, both of which are returned by `dbListTables()`, see #27 & #29. 

See [this thread](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/flat/CAH7T-ao6ece1mgCsCvsE04W59ZZJP9gGXVK97wkUzRV5gsDqQQ%40mail.gmail.com) on the psql-hackers list for a discussion on why they are not in the `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.tables` (which includes Views). Tl;dr: "They are not defined by the SQL standard." I see this as a relatively minor point w.r.t. RPostgres, though. 

As it stands there is no helper function like `dbListTables()` to list Materialized Views in RPostgres. 

The following query shows all Tables, Views and Materialized Views (I have not looked into temporary tables, yet): 

```sql
SELECT tablename AS name FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = ANY (current_schemas(false))
UNION
SELECT viewname AS name FROM pg_views WHERE schemaname = ANY (current_schemas(false))
UNION
SELECT matviewname as name FROM pg_matviews WHERE schemaname = ANY (current_schemas(false))
ORDER BY name;
```

title: `timezone` connection argument ignored when casting a date string
description:
If I am not mistaken, the `timezone` argument of the connection is ignored when casting a date string to a `timestamp with timezone`.

``` r
library(DBI)
Sys.timezone()
#> [1] "Europe/Berlin"
query <- "SELECT '2020-05-04'::TIMESTAMPTZ;"

con <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname="postgres", timezone = "America/Chicago")
dbGetQuery(con, "SHOW TIMEZONE;")
#>          TimeZone
#> 1 America/Chicago
res <- dbGetQuery(con, query)
res
#>           timestamptz
#> 1 2020-05-04 02:00:00
res[[1,1]]
#> [1] "2020-05-04 02:00:00 CEST"
dbDisconnect(con)
```

With #222 in mind, it seems that this is returned as `2020-05-04 00:00:00` in UTC and then a +2 hour offset for my `Sys.timezone()` is added.

The offset from ‘America/Chicago’ to ‘Europe/Berlin’ is usually +7 hours, so IMHO this should either return `2020-05-04 00:00:00 CDT` or `2020-05-04 07:00:00 CEST`?

When setting a different timezone for the connection, I get the same output.

``` r
con <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname="postgres", timezone = "Europe/London")
dbGetQuery(con, "SHOW TIMEZONE;")
#>        TimeZone
#> 1 Europe/London
res <- dbGetQuery(con, query)
res
#>           timestamptz
#> 1 2020-05-04 02:00:00
res[[1,1]]
#> [1] "2020-05-04 02:00:00 CEST"
dbDisconnect(con)
```


`psql` shows this:

```sql
postgres=# SET TIMEZONE TO 'America/Chicago';
SET
postgres=# SHOW TIMEZONE;
    TimeZone
-----------------
 America/Chicago
(1 Zeile)


postgres=# SELECT '2020-05-04'::TIMESTAMPTZ;
      timestamptz
------------------------
 2020-05-04 00:00:00-05
(1 Zeile)
```

title: as.POSIXct() to Postgres timestamptz round trip does not behave as expected
description:
Based on how RPostgres reads timestamptz formatted fields, I woulda expected different behavior when writing to the database. The below example runs on a docker container based on the postgrel:latest image. 

The following is correctly returned as CET, which is UTC+1 (January is within winter time). 

```r
as.POSIXct("2020-01-01 12:00:00", tz = "Europe/Zurich")
#> [1] "2020-01-01 12:00:00 CET"
```

When I write this to a PostgreSQL `timestamptz` field

```r
dbExecute(con, "CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE bla(id integer, some_time TIMESTAMPTZ)")
dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO bla VALUES (1, $1)", as.POSIXct("2020-01-01 12:00:00", tz = "Europe/Zurich"))
dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO bla VALUES (2, '2020-01-01 12:00:00+01')")
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM bla")
```
will return (in R)

id           some_time
 1       2020-01-01 13:00:00
 2      2020-01-01 12:00:00

So what happened? Both inserts end up being stored in the DB's `timestamptz` field as UTC, in other words tz seems to be ignored. That behavior would be somewhat ok though it may waste some time on larger datasets ( it would simply mean I had to convert everything to UTC in R before storing). But what puzzles me is that READING data obviously respects the local time zone and resurrects the time zone... 

In other words, I don't think we should have difference here: 

direct SQL query on a psql client
```SQL
postgres=# SELECT * FROM bla ;
 id |       some_time        
----+------------------------
  1 | 2020-01-01 12:00:00+00
  2 | 2020-01-01 11:00:00+00
(2 rows)
```
vs R


```r

> dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM bla")
  id           some_time
1  1 2020-01-01 13:00:00
2  2 2020-01-01 12:00:00

```

Is it me or this is a bug / odd 🤷‍♂️  ?

title: dbColumnInfo doesn't match DBI spec
description:
I'm trying to port some code over that uses the RPostgreSQL driver; I need to be able check the actual SQL/Postgres variable type. The DBI man page for dbColumnInfo states "Methods MUST include name, field.type (the SQL type), and data.type (the R data type) columns"

RPostgres currently returns just "name" and "type" which matches "data.type" (i.e., the R data type). Any chance to move towards DBI and compatibility with RPostgreSQL? 

For what its worth RPostgreSQL also uses the column name "type" but uses it for "field.type" so they will collide while RMySQL has the same behavior leaving RPostgres as the outlier.

title: Support LISTEN/NOTIFY
description:
To be able to receive notifications from Postgres' NOTIFY/LISTEN there needs to be a method to read from ``PQnotifies()``. There's a C example showing how it works here: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-example.html#LIBPQ-EXAMPLE-2

I've made a rough first-pass at implementing it here - https://github.com/lentinj/RPostgres/commit/4b138b1abb1a5e5699502edec79bef34bfe45eef - this adds a ``pqWaitForNotify()`` that sleeps a given number of seconds, or until there's a message.

My main question is where to hang the functionality. Adding a method to DBI, then implementing here seems the wrong thing to do, as this is Postgres specific. Is there an interface you'd prefer instead of what's above?


```
^C
```

title: RPostgres-specific strInterpolate, sqlAppendTableTemplate
description:
RPostgres accepts parameters with `$1`, `$2`. The function from DBI assumes `?1`, `?2` format.
### Expected Behavior:

When used, the functions should provide dbengine-specific for parameter indexing. That is, for RSQLite, one of `?`, `?1`, or `:name`; for RPostgres, `$1`; for RSQLServer `?` (limited by jTDS). Because I don't expect `DBI` to track all other engines' mechanisms, I would expect this method to be overridden by each driver.
### Actual Behavior:

``` r
connpg <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
dbWriteTable(connpg, "mtcars", mtcars[1,], row.names = FALSE)
# [1] TRUE
(qry <- sqlAppendTableTemplate(connpg, "mtcars", mtcars[,3:5], row.names = FALSE))
# <SQL> INSERT INTO "mtcars"
#   ("disp", "hp", "drat")
# VALUES
#   (?1, ?2, ?3)
res <- dbSendQuery(connpg, qry)
# Error: ERROR:  operator does not exist: ? integer
# LINE 4:   (?1, ?2, ?3)
```

dbExistsTable does not honor case of table name
description:
### Problem:

`dbExistsTable` is inconsistent with regards to case of table names.
### Expected

Because postgres down-cases identifiers by default (the use of `dbQuoteIdentifier` is the exception), I expect that queries for unquoted mixed-case table names to still compare successfully with their down-cased name in the database.
### Actual

Unquoted, I expect all searches for mixed-case table names to match the lower-case:

``` r
tblnm <- "foobar"
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf("create table %s (id serial8 primary key, num integer)", tblnm))
# [1] 0
dbExistsTable(connpg, "foobar") # correct
# [1] TRUE
dbExistsTable(connpg, "Foobar") # incorrect
# [1] FALSE
dbExistsTable(connpg, dbQuoteIdentifier(connpg, tblnm)) # incorrect
# [1] FALSE
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf('drop table if exists %s', tblnm))
# [1] 0
```

Unquoted, down-cased within postgres:

``` r
tblnm <- "Foobar"
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf("create table %s (id serial8 primary key, num integer)", tblnm))
# [1] 0
dbExistsTable(connpg, "foobar") # correct
# [1] TRUE
dbExistsTable(connpg, "Foobar") # incorrect
# [1] FALSE
dbExistsTable(connpg, dbQuoteIdentifier(connpg, tblnm)) # correct
# [1] FALSE
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf('drop table if exists %s', tblnm))
# [1] 0
```

Quoted on definition, this should be the most-specific:

``` r
tblnm <- dbQuoteIdentifier(connpg, "Foobar")
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf("create table %s (id serial8 primary key, num integer)", tblnm))
# [1] 0
dbExistsTable(connpg, "foobar") # correct
# [1] FALSE
dbExistsTable(connpg, "Foobar") # incorrect
# [1] TRUE
dbExistsTable(connpg, tblnm) # incorrect
# [1] FALSE
dbExecute(connpg, sprintf('drop table if exists %s', tblnm))
# [1] 0
```

description:
We don't allow password authentication to our postgres database, and use certificates and keys instead. I have something that works just fine when I use RPostgreSQL, but does not work with RPostgres:

`this_works <- dbConnect ( RPostgreSQL::PostgreSQL(), 
host =  "111.22.33.44", user = "pm", 
dbname = "dbname = thedb sslcert=pm.crt sslkey=pm.key")`

Although, honestly, it's a bit awkward with the whole `dbname = "dbname = thedb..."` 

However, I cannot find any permutation that works with **RPostgres**. These all fail, complaining about not being able to find pg_hba.conf entries:

```
this_fails <- dbConnect ( RPostgres::Postgres(), host =  "111.22.33.44", user = "pm", dbname = "thedb sslcert=pm.crt sslkey=pm.key")
Error in eval(substitute(expr), envir, enclos) :

FATAL:  pg_hba.conf rejects connection for host "123.45.67.89", user "pm", database "fnma_edna sslcert=pm.crt sslkey=pm.key", SSL off
```

This also fails
```
this_also_fails <- dbConnect ( RPostgres::Postgres(), host =  "111.22.33.44", user = "pm", dbname = "dbname = thedb sslcert=pm.crt sslkey=pm.key")
```

title: Parameterized queries not working with NULL values
description:
# Summary

NULL and zero-length vectors (e.g. character(0) ) cause an error when used as parameters in a parameterized query. 
# Expected Behaviour

I haven't found RPostgres documentation that states explicitly what an R NULL should produce on the query end, but a database NULL seems reasonable. If this is too difficult, some other way telling the database to use NULL as a query parameter would be very beneficial.
# Actual Behaviour

Here's a toy example:

In PostgreSQL:

```
create table foo (ival int, tval text, bval bytea);
```

In R:

This works:

```
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "INSERT INTO foo VALUES($1, $2, $3)", 
                   params=list(ival=1, 
                               tval= 'not quite null',
                               bval=charToRaw('asdf')
                               )
                    )
```

But this throws an error:

```
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "INSERT INTO foo VALUES($1, $2, $3)",
                   params=list(ival=NULL, 
                               tval= 'not quite null',
                               bval=charToRaw('asdf')
                               )
                   )
```

Using RPostgres, the error message is:

> Error: expecting a string

The error message is the same with NULL for tval or bval.

Thanks for your attention on this matter.

Regards

Jason

title: POSIXt uploads affected by options("digits.secs")
description:
The precision of the timestamp inserted into the database is affected by the display option, `"digits.secs"`. Likely related to #53, #61, and #104.

## Expected behavior

The use of `"digits.secs"` should only affect the *display* of `POSIXt` values, not the precision of values inserted into the database.

## Actual behavior

Precision is lost on inserted data, using both `dbWriteTable` and `dbBind`.

## Reproducible example

Done here with `TIMESTAMP`, behaves the same using `TIMESTAMPTZ`.

```r
now <- Sys.time()
dbExecute(conn, "create table quux ( tm timestamp )")

options(digits.secs = 0) # the default
now
# [1] "2017-07-19 09:51:23 PDT"
dbWriteTable(conn, "quux", data.frame(tm = now), append = TRUE)
# [1] TRUE
res <- dbSendQuery(conn, "insert into quux (tm) values ($1)")
dbBind(res, params = list(now))
dbClearResult(res)
# [1] TRUE
dbGetQuery(conn, "select tm from quux")
#                    tm
# 1 2017-07-19 09:51:23
# 2 2017-07-19 09:51:23

options(digits.secs = 6)
now
# [1] "2017-07-19 09:51:23.840996 PDT"
dbWriteTable(conn, "quux", data.frame(tm = now), append = TRUE)
# [1] TRUE
res <- dbSendQuery(conn, "insert into quux (tm) values ($1)")
dbBind(res, params = list(now))
dbClearResult(res)
# [1] TRUE
dbGetQuery(conn, "select tm from quux")
#                           tm
# 1        2017-07-19 09:51:23
# 2        2017-07-19 09:51:23
# 3 2017-07-19 09:51:23.840996
# 4 2017-07-19 09:51:23.840996
```

(The returned `tm` is class `character`, un-converted for this example.)

An easy workaround for me is to do something like:

```r
op <- options(digits.secs = 6)
on.exit(options(op), add = TRUE)
```

in any function dealing with timestamps in the database.

title: can't write timestamps using RPostgres dbWriteTable
description:
I'm trying to write an R `tibble` object (or data.frame) into a Postgres database using the RPostgres package. Following the documentation, I'm trying to use the `dbWriteTable` function.

However, I realized that there's no specification of `field.types` in the method. Here I provide a minimal example where you can see the method failing when the input has a `POSIXct` timestamp (and passing when it is interpreted as a character). 

```
library(dplyr)
library(DBI)
library(RPostgres)
library(tibble)

conn <- dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
  host = url$host,
  port = url$port,
  dbname = url$dbname,
  user = url$user,
  password = url$password
)

test <- tibble(
  words = c("hallo","ja", "nein"),
  value = c(3,4,5),
  time= as.POSIXct(c("2016-05-04 04:32","2016-06-02 09:37","2016-07-12 10:43"))
)
test2 <- tibble(
  words = c("hallo","ja", "nein"),
  value = c(3,4,5),
  time= c("2016-05-04 04:32","2016-06-02 09:37","2016-07-12 10:43")
)

dbWriteTable(conn = conn, name = "words", value = test)
> Error in eval(substitute(expr), envir, enclos) :
> ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type real: "2016-05-04 04:32:00"
> CONTEXT:  COPY words, line 1, column time: "2016-05-04 04:32:00"

dbWriteTable(conn = conn, name = "words2", value = test2)
> [1] TRUE
```

Would merging this PR https://github.com/rstats-db/RPostgres/pull/45 solve this issue, or is a deeper integration required?

title: bytea columns have incorrect deserialization to raw vector
description:
When RPostgres reads a column of `bytea` type, it deserializes the data into a raw vector by converting the _string representation_ of the data as returned by postgres to a raw vector instead of parsing the postgres hex format for bytea columns. 

As as example, the following result is incorrect:

``` R
> res.show.bug <- dbSendQuery(con, "with test as (select '\x0a'::bytea) select * from test")
> res.result <- dbFetch(res.show.bug)
> res.result
           bytea
1 5c, 78, 30, 61
> rawToChar(res.result$bytea[[1]])
[1] "\\x0a"
```

The result should clearly be (to follow POTS) equal to `as.raw(as.hexmode("0a"))`, which can be yielded from `res.result` above by applying this transformation (using `hex2raw` from the `wkb` package):

``` R
> hex2raw(rawToChar(res.result$bytea[[1]]))
[1] 0a
```

title: Include views in listed tables?
description:
This is also in hadley/dplyr#1007 (because it comes up when using the `tbl` function). I'm mentioning it here because it seems like RPostgres is going to replace RPostgreSQL eventually and might be able to fix the problem.

RPostgreSQL doesn't return views when using `dbListTables`, which is unexpected for some users. RPostgres uses the same query:

``` SQL
select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname !='information_schema' and schemaname !='pg_catalog';
```

I'm not sure whether RPostgres should just return views along with the tables, or whether there should be a separate `dbListViews` function. But I feel like there should be some way to get at them without writing a raw query.

The following gets both views and "real" tables:

``` SQL
SELECT table_name FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.tables WHERE table_schema = ANY (current_schemas(false));
```

```R
dbExecute(con, "CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fuutab
```
